A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FieldFormer, retaining its local-transformer foundation and three simulation benchmarks despite substantial revisions. Text, equations, figures and tables support comparison throughout. v1 has no appendices; v2's Appendices A–D are readable and included.

before.justification: Section 4 and Table 1 report original reconstruction experiments on heat, shallow-water and pollution simulations.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D report original simulation and real-world monitoring experiments, including sensor-holdout evaluations and architectural ablations.

M1.justification: v1 dynamically selects neighborhoods through velocity-reweighted offset tables and EM-style updates. v2 Section 4.2 specifies fixed sparse candidate contexts with learned scales applied to token offsets. It also adds coordinate-dependent Gamma Fields and makes the original physics-regularized formulation an optional FieldFormer-PINN variant. Section 4.3 nevertheless retains inconsistent offset-selection language.

E1.justification: The three simulation benchmarks remain. v2 adds actual Delhi pollution monitoring, targeting PM10 and PM2.5, and atmospheric monitoring, targeting temperature, humidity and two wind components. These use hourly observations from 32 stations over May 2018–November 2020 and substantially extend empirical coverage beyond simulated fields.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates SVGP and physics-regularized SIREN/Fourier-MLP while excluding grid-based comparators. v2 evaluates adapted RecFNO, ImputeFormer and Senseiver on the retained benchmarks, and separately reports plain and PINN versions of the neural-field baselines. Physics-regularized neural fields themselves were already present in v1.

E3.justification: v2 introduces whole-sensor holdout evaluation, distinct from withholding observations at existing sensors, and specifies new comparator-specific rasterization and masked-window procedures. It retains sensor/full-field RMSE and MAE but removes normalized PDE residuals from the evaluation metrics. The newly disclosed split ratio for existing experiments does not establish that their splits changed.

E4.justification: v1 contains no component ablation study. v2 Tables 5–8 test physics regularization, transformer versus MLP aggregation, and global versus coordinate-dependent scaling across sensor-space, full-field and holdout settings. Appendix D adds evidence about whether Gamma Fields help generalization to unseen sensors.

E5.justification: Both versions report bootstrap mean ± standard deviation for sensor metrics. v2 newly specifies 1000 bootstrap samples and adds uncertainty values to full-field results in Tables 3 and 6, where v1 reported point estimates. The full-field uncertainty procedure remains unclear, and neither version establishes additional independent training runs.

E6.justification: The retained benchmarks receive substantially different numerical results. For example, v1 Table 1 reports SWE sensor RMSE 0.001113 for physics-regularized FieldFormer; v2 Table 5 reports 0.05716 for FieldFormer-PINN and 0.04644 for unregularized FieldFormer. Method and protocol equivalence is not established, so these are revised results rather than demonstrated same-setting performance changes. Real-data, holdout and ablation outcomes are also added.

T1.justification: The principal theorem statements and locality/sampling assumptions are largely retained. However, Appendix C replaces proof sketches with substantially expanded tokenization, compactness and symmetrization arguments. Section 3 adds formal global-field and sensor-space objectives, and v1's incorrect derivative-sign calculation is removed. These changes go beyond relocating existing theory.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes physically consistent global field reconstruction, claiming consistent improvements exceeding 40%. v2 centers locality-aware prediction over persistent sensor networks and makes non-identifiability of global reconstruction a central contribution. Its introduction and conclusion explicitly reject universal global-reconstruction superiority and treat physics regularization as optional.

C2.justification: v2 interprets reconstruction quality through observational support and alignment between model priors and the data, substantially expanding v1's limitations discussion. It explains weaker unseen-sensor performance, possible conflicts between physics penalties and noisy observations, and nonuniform benefits from Gamma Fields. These materially qualify the earlier favorable account of physics-guided reconstruction.

D1.justification: v2 adds substantial implementation and evaluation documentation: baseline adaptations, 80/10/10 splits, exclusion of held-out observations from training contexts, training-only normalization, masks, AdamW, gradient clipping and early stopping. For retained experiments, these are newly disclosed details rather than established setting changes. Some earlier simulator details disappear, including the 3.5 m/s base wind, time-compression factor and specific data-source references.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially reframed around sparse observability, identifiability and architectural priors. v2 adds identifiability references such as Norden et al. and Wieland et al., alongside Senseiver, RecFNO and additional graph-based work. It replaces v1's categorical dismissal of mesh-dependent comparators with discussion and evaluation of their adaptations.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work and conclusion are extensively rewritten. v2 introduces standalone problem-formulation and theoretical-insight sections, reorganizes evaluation by prediction regime, and moves boundary losses, formal assumptions and proofs into appendices. This is substantial narrative and structural revision.

P2.justification: v1's single combined results table is replaced by eight tables organized around prediction regimes and ablations, with substantially different row/column structures. Figure 1 reuses the same graphic but is enlarged, relocated and given a revised caption. Title, author-block and heading layouts also change; several new wide tables use very small type.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical credibility through real monitoring data, previously excluded strong comparators, unseen-sensor testing and component ablations. Its main discussion better distinguishes successful sensor imputation from unreliable global recovery, addressing central weaknesses in v1's broad superiority claims. Important problems remain: Sections 4.2–4.3 conflict about neighborhood construction, and Appendix C.2 does not justify transferring its randomized-input risk bound to the original data distribution. These limit the revision's rigor but do not outweigh the substantial empirical and interpretive gains.
